title: Daily Debrief — Wednesday Nov 11, 2026
html:
CoreWeave's numbers lit up the chips, and SPY took back half its October drop. Here's what I'm seeing. One strong earnings report from an AI cloud company calmed this week's fear: chip stocks jumped 5.7%, SPY gained 1.3%, and the SPY call on the scorecard hit its target.

The one thing

SPY reclaimed its 50% line at $757.17 and stopped just under the $763–765 ceiling. Above $765, the road opens to $771. A close back under $751.39 says today was only a relief bounce.

CoreWeave, a company that rents out Nvidia chips to AI builders, grew revenue 168% to $3.7 billion and raised its profit outlook. Its stock jumped 24.7%, and the fear that AI spending is drying up eased. The Philadelphia chip index rose 5.7% and tech was the best of the 11 sectors (+2.7%).

SPY rose 1.3% to $759.81 (the S&P 500 closed at 7,619), the Nasdaq gained 1.6%, and the VIX fear gauge fell for a fourth day to 17.49. Apple closed at a record ($355.63). The bond market was shut for Veterans Day, so rates got no test today; futures still fully price a December rate hike, with about a 10% chance of a half-point.

SPY in one picture

How I read it: the high, $762.51, stopped 43 cents under the 61.8% line of the Oct 6 → Nov 5 drop ($762.94), with the 50-day average ($764.55) right above it. That's the ceiling, $763–765. The 50% line at $757.17 is now the first support. A close over $765 points to $771.15, then the record. A close under $751.39 puts SPY back in last week's box.

Lesson of the day: Rotation: when money changes rooms

The market can rise and still hurt a stock you own, because money doesn't only come in or go out. It also moves from one room to another. Big funds trim what has run and buy what has fallen, and on days like today you can watch it happen.

Over the past month travel was the winner (RCL +19%, DAL +15%, HLT +14%) and chips the loser (DELL −35%, MU −15%, SMH −14%). Today one good chip report flipped it: chips up 5.7%, DELL and MU up about 12%, while ABNB, RCL, DAL and HLT all fell on a green day for SPY.

What it means: when DAL sags on a day like this, it's the rotation, not news about Delta. Judge it by its levels ($88.18, then the $83 stop), not by the red number. And don't chase the first day of a rotation: MU and BE are still under their 50-day averages, and first-day pops in a downtrend often give a lot back. Wait for the pullback to a level.

Fib in action: downside extensions (Fibonacci Playbook)

How far can a drop run? Nvidia's downside extension

A downside extension projects where a fall may run out of fuel. It uses three points: A = where the drop started, B = the first low, C = the bounce that failed. Level = C − (A − B) × ratio.

Anchors: A = the Oct 6 high $243.37 (the top of the year's run), B = the Oct 23 low $210.18, C = the Oct 28 bounce $219.99. A − B = $33.19. Math: 1.382 = 219.99 − 33.19 × 1.382 = $174.12. 1.618 = 219.99 − 33.19 × 1.618 = $166.29. 2.0 = 219.99 − 66.38 = $153.61.

What price did: Tuesday's low $165.89 pierced the 1.618 by 40 cents and closed back above it. Today Nvidia bounced 2.9%; the high $177.54 broke over the 1.382 and the close $173.73 slipped back under it. For a trade: the 1.618 is where a put buyer takes profit. A close over $174.12 flips it to support (next $180.91); a call there would use a stop just under $163.90. Below $163.90, the 2.0 at $153.61 is the target.

Try it: with the same A, B and C, where are Nvidia's 2.382 and 2.618 extensions?

  • C · Oct 28 bounce: $219.99
  • B · Oct 23 low: $210.18
  • 1.0 ext (equal move): $186.80
  • 1.382 ext · today's wick: $174.12
  • 1.618 ext · Tue low $165.89: $166.29
  • 2.0 ext: $153.61
  • NOW: $173.73

Answers to the try-it: 2.382 = 219.99 − 33.19 × 2.382 = $140.93; 2.618 = $133.10.
